compiled_state.title: As an operator auditing a remediation loop after the fact, I want each cycle atomically appended to the touchpoint's review artifact under a cycles[] array with graceful migration and a single ticket-comment reference
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Description

**What**: Implement SC5's cross-cutting persistence: a shared atomic-append writer utility for the cycles[] array on each touchpoint's existing review artifact, graceful initialization to [] when reading an artifact that lacks the key, and a single-ticket-comment policy referencing the artifact path (not duplicating cycle bodies in the ticket). Used by preplanning Phase E, impl-plan Steps 2/4/6, and sprint verifier-fail. Cycle entries follow the exact schema {n, draft_hash, findings_count, verdict, timestamp_iso}.

**Why**: SC5 — without atomic append + the exact schema + draft_hash field, the oscillation-check hard gate from SC4 loses its structural-diff anchor.

**Scope**:
- IN: Shared writer utility (atomic-append via temp-then-rename or file-locking)
- IN: Graceful migration logic for in-flight artifacts lacking cycles[]
- IN: Integration of writer at all 4 touchpoints (Phase E, impl-plan Steps 2/4/6, sprint verifier-fail)
- IN: Three SC5 fixtures: per-touchpoint review-artifact extension, concurrent-write fixture, migration fixture
- IN: Single-ticket-comment policy at each touchpoint
- OUT: Producer DELTA OUTPUT shape (depended on — the writer hashes producer output)

## Done Definitions

- A shared writer utility performs atomic append to the cycles[] array on the touchpoint's existing review artifact. Each entry contains EXACTLY these five fields: n (int), draft_hash (sha256 of producer's DELTA OUTPUT block — not of the ticket payload), findings_count (int), verdict (enum), timestamp_iso (RFC3339). Fixture asserts field presence, types, and that draft_hash is computed over the producer's emitted draft
  ← Satisfies: sc-5
- When the existing review artifact lacks the cycles key, the writer initializes it to [] before appending (graceful migration) and does not overwrite other artifact fields
  ← Satisfies: sc-5
- Each touchpoint's existing review-artifact test, extended to assert the cycles[] array, passes for preplanning Phase E, impl-plan Steps 2/4/6, and sprint verifier-fail sites
  ← Satisfies: sc-5
- Concurrent-write fixture passes: two concurrent writers each appending one cycle entry result in cycles[] containing both entries (no lost writes)
  ← Satisfies: sc-5
- Migration fixture passes: an artifact pre-existing without cycles[] is read, cycles[] is initialized to [], and the first append yields cycles[] of length 1
  ← Satisfies: sc-5
- At each touchpoint, a single ticket comment per remediation cycle references the artifact path (not the cycle body)
  ← Satisfies: sc-5

## Considerations

- [Concurrency] Atomic-append must be implemented via file-locking or atomic-rename (write to temp then rename); naive read-modify-write is not safe under concurrent writers.
- [Backward compatibility] Existing review artifacts without cycles[] must be readable by all consumers after migration; do not require migration scripts.
- [Observability] The single-ticket-comment policy aligns with the SC1/SC2/SC3/SC4 caller-side stories, which each record one comment per dispatch — coordinate the comment format so it points to the same artifact.
- [Contract / draft_hash] draft_hash is a contract that bridges the producers (SC1/SC2/SC3 producer-contract stories) and this writer. The writer MUST hash the producer's DELTA OUTPUT block, not the ticket payload. If the producer shapes change, draft_hash semantics change — coordinate via the shared protocol doc.

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
